findings.claim: Planetary Science is a first-class comparative planetary-systems domain bridging astronomy and Earth/geoscience, but not yet an independent canonical major region.
Biochemistry, Microbiology, Developmental Biology and Physiology are stable life-science identities with different bridge/process/function roles; none requires wholesale root promotion.

Engineering specialties are best represented as explicit major subspaces/intervention bridges under the broader Engineering/Design topology, not as peer foundational regions by institutional symmetry.
Philosophy of Mind is a major philosophical subspace and cognition bridge; Philology is a historical-language/textual bridge and method axis.
Food Science is a stable applied/composite domain spanning chemistry, biology, microbiology, engineering and human/nutrition boundaries rather than a foundational major region.
All 17 residual candidates from the v0 broad census are now explicitly normalized; this closes only that bounded residual set, not the open-world foundational census.

internalLensSemantics: Internal lenses constrain modeling and generate negative controls; external evidence remains independently required for every normalized space.

normalizedSpaces.label: Planetary science
normalizedSpaces.rationale: AGU defines planetary science around properties, formation and evolution of planetary bodies and environments from cores to magnetospheres, using geophysical/geochemical principles and observational, experimental and modeling approaches. This supports a first-class comparative planetary systems identity, not reduction to Astronomy or Earth Science.

normalizedSpaces.label: Biochemistry
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ASBMB distinguishes biochemistry as investigation of molecular composition and chemical reactions in life while treating BMB as enabling molecular-life science. Biochemistry is therefore a stable Chemistry↔Life bridge, not identical to Molecular Biology.

normalizedSpaces.label: Microbiology / microbial sciences
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ASM spans fundamental, clinical and applied microbial sciences across health, environment, agriculture and industry. Microbiology has stable object/regime identity around microbial life, but its applications and bridges do not justify a separate foundational major region by themselves.

normalizedSpaces.label: Developmental biology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: SDB describes developmental biology through mechanisms of development, differentiation and growth at molecular, cellular, genetic and evolutionary levels. Development is a cross-scale biological process axis plus major subspace, not a new root.

normalizedSpaces.label: Physiology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: APS characterizes physiology as broad scientific inquiry into biological function of living organisms and foundational to life sciences. Function crosses organs, systems, organisms and health contexts, supporting a major functional/system axis rather than a primitive root.

normalizedSpaces.label: Philosophy of mind and cognition
normalizedSpaces.rationale: University philosophy research structures treat philosophy of mind as a stable philosophical area with explicit links to psychology, cognitive science, epistemology, metaphysics and language. It is a major conceptual bridge/subspace rather than a separate foundational region.

normalizedSpaces.label: Mechanical engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ABET requires mechanical programs to combine engineering/basic science/mathematics with modeling, analysis, design and realization of physical, thermal and mechanical systems. This is a major engineering specialization, not an independent foundational major region.

normalizedSpaces.label: Electrical and electronic engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ABET treats electrical/electronic programs as engineering specializations spanning devices, software-containing systems, communication and advanced mathematics. Preserve as major engineering subspace with multiple bridges.

normalizedSpaces.label: Civil and structural engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ABET civil criteria combine physical/basic sciences, design and system-scale ecological/social impacts. This is a built-environment intervention specialization under Engineering, not a foundational object science.

normalizedSpaces.label: Chemical engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ABET chemical-engineering criteria center material/energy balances, thermodynamics, transport, reaction, process control and design. It is a Chemistry↔Engineering process-intervention bridge, distinct from Chemistry itself.

normalizedSpaces.label: Computer engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ABET treats computer engineering within electrical/computer engineering with hardware/software system design and discrete mathematics. It is a realization bridge between computation and engineered electronic systems, not Computational Possibility or theoretical computing.

normalizedSpaces.label: Software engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ABET software criteria emphasize design/construction, requirements, verification/validation and processes/tools for complex software systems. Software Engineering is an applied realization discipline, not a foundational computation identity.

normalizedSpaces.label: Control engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ABET places control across chemical, electrical/electronic, mechatronic and systems engineering contexts. Control Engineering applies systems/control theory as an intervention discipline and should not duplicate the formal Systems Theory & Control identity.

normalizedSpaces.label: Environmental engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: ABET environmental criteria explicitly integrate chemistry, Earth science, biology, fluid mechanics, fate/transport and engineered systems. It is a multi-foundation intervention bridge, not a foundational region.

normalizedSpaces.label: Energy engineering
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Energy engineering draws on multiple engineering and physical/material domains. Current evidence supports an applied intervention bridge; no deletion-essential independent foundational identity has been shown.

normalizedSpaces.label: Philology
normalizedSpaces.rationale: Oxford defines philology around systematic behavior and development of languages over time, overlapping many linguistic fields; WPU emphasizes oral/written language and literary heritage. Philology is a historical-language/textual bridge and method axis, not a primitive humanities root.

normalizedSpaces.label: Food science
normalizedSpaces.rationale: IFST defines food science through physical, biological and chemical properties plus processing, preservation, safety and quality; IFT describes the field as multidisciplinary. It is a stable applied/composite science of food, not a new foundational major region.

policies.engineeringRule: Engineering specializations remain explicit identities but default to major subspace/intervention roles unless deletion-essential independent major-region structure is proven.
policies.internalTheoryFirewall: Ordivon owner theory cannot count as external evidence for field existence or standing.
policies.subordinationAllowed: A stable field may normalize as a major subspace, bridge, axis, applied/translational or composite without manufacturing a major region.
